gen-dafont-brusher-fs-spline-sans: Loose brushwork, all romance and motion. Brusher swings its heavy, cord-like curves above Spline Sans, a sans-serif whose wide gaps and level strokes make a quiet, comfortable footing in small doses.
gen-dafont-brusher-fs-synonym: Synonym keeps its ink in one plain stripe, with generous openings in every curve. Brusher is the one for flourish, a calligraphic hand with a wide-open e, while Synonym does the steady work of being comfortable in small doses.
gen-dafont-brusher-plus-jakarta-sans: Ink-heavy flourish up top, precise lines below. Brusher carries a romantic calligraphic hand, and Plus Jakarta Sans follows in monoline strokes with curve endings kept well apart, though shrinking the heading would blur its heavy cord-like curves.
gen-dafont-brusher-sora: Sora reads precise and geometric, with a c and s kept widely parted. Brusher's romantic, heavy-curved script against that unpressured sans is the pair's strongest quality, and it suits brief copy best.
gen-dafont-burnstown-dam-fs-karma: Karma is a trustworthy serif whose terminals finish well clear of the stem, with little gap between x-height and cap height. Over a longer passage its mild modulation never snags the eye.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-abeezee: Neon-tube lettering, widely spaced and expressive. Bushcraft's closed, single-weight shapes sit over ABeeZee, a plain sans with open terminals and a high mean line that gives the page somewhere gentler to land.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-aldrich: Expressive Bushcraft sets its extra-wide, single-weight letters up top, closed and artistic. Aldrich follows in a plain sans with cupped round letters and a tall x-height, so a longer passage feels like tracing one thick thread.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-alexandria: Wide-spaced, flat-lined lettering from Bushcraft, where capitals barely rise above the lowercase and every curve keeps one weight. Alexandria, a sans-serif with open c terminals, is its relief.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-amiko: Amiko reads modern and neutral, its crayon-tall lowercase strokes ending in terminals that flare outward like tongs. But Bushcraft does the showing off, with closed, extra-wide letters, while Amiko, a sans-serif, does the talking.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-anek-bangla: Glowing neon-tube letters, spaced wide. Bushcraft is the artistic showpiece with its closed, single-track strokes, while Anek Bangla, a sans, quietly handles the text with wide, barely curled s curves and short ascenders.
